heroHeadline: Cité Soleil Hospitals Evacuated After Gang Violence Surge; PM Fils-Aimé Casts Doubt on August Elections
heroSubtitle: Gang fighting erupting in Cité Soleil and the Cul-de-Sac Plain on May 10 forced MSF to evacuate its hospital — the only emergency medical facility for 300,000 residents living under total gang control — after treating more than 40 gunshot victims in 12 hours. The Centre Hospitalier de Fontaine also suspended operations, evacuating 11 newborns from its neonatal ICU. As of May 13, the MSF hospital remains closed. Concurrent intra-Viv Ansanm gang clashes on the Cul-de-Sac Plain pitted Duvivier/Pyè 6 factions against Chen Mechan, Taliban, and 400 Mawozo groups — killing at least 8 and displacing hundreds to thousands — as rival factions fight over cargo truck extortion routes supplying Port-au-Prince. Hundreds of displaced families were photographed sheltering on the road to Toussaint Louverture International Airport. In the most explicit government acknowledgment yet that Haiti's August 30, 2026 election timeline is in jeopardy, PM Alix Didier Fils-Aimé stated that 'conditions must allow voters to choose freely' — with no electoral decree issued, no voter registration begun, and 23 communes still inaccessible. The GSF advance force of approximately 545 personnel continues to focus exclusively on Port-au-Prince city-center joint operations, leaving Cité Soleil and the entire Artibonite Department without international security coverage. 1.47M+ Haitians remain internally displaced; 5.8M face acute food insecurity; the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains funded at only ~20% of its $880M target.
